mainTopic: How a בדיקה limits retroactive טומאה, and זעירי's ruling that the מעת לעת period makes a bed and seat טמא
overview: The גמרא first explains why the משנה had to say that a בדיקה shortens even the short time since her last examination. We might have thought the רבנן worried about ruining טהרות only over a full מעת לעת. Next it asks why the משנה's case of דיה שעתה mentions a bed. It answers that the detail teaches that retroactive מעת לעת טומאה makes the bed טמא, which supports זעירי. The גמרא then asks how a bed, which cannot be 'asked', can become טמא through a doubt. It gives two answers: her friends were carrying the bed, or, following רבי יוחנן, a doubt caused by a person counts as 'can be asked' anyway. רבי יוחנן's rule is tested against a ברייתא about a man wrapping himself in his cloak, and the גמרא answers that the ברייתא is about רשות הרבים. Finally, זעירי's ruling is challenged from אבימי's ברייתא, which says her bed is 'like her touch'. רבא defends זעירי with a קל וחומר from a sealed clay vessel. The גמרא begins to reread the ברייתא, and the reading continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Why teach that a בדיקה shortens the shorter period?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה bothered to say that a בדיקה cuts down the period מפקידה לפקידה, which already seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a בדיקה shortens even the long 24-hour period, do we really need to be told that it shortens the period from one examination to the next?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge. It asks why the משנה needed to say that a בדיקה shortens the period מפקידה לפקידה, when this seems obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a בדיקה shortens both the מעת לעת period and the מפקידה לפקידה period. If it can shorten the longer 24-hour span, it should obviously shorten the shorter span between examinations. So the second half of the משנה looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: An examination with a cloth to check for blood
From one examination to the next, the time since her last clean check
A full 24-hour period counted backward
Is it necessary? Used to say something seems too obvious to teach

phrases.english: Is it necessary to teach that it shortens from examination to examination?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the גמרא's question about the wording of the משנה, which began before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that a בדיקה shortens the period מפקידה לפקידה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר logic: if a בדיקה shortens the longer 24-hour period, it surely shortens the shorter period, so the משנה's words seem extra.

steps.title: The concern for losing טהרות might apply only to the longer period
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that we might have thought the רבנן cared about lost טהרות only over a full מעת לעת, so the משנה had to teach that the rule also applies מפקידה לפקידה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that only for the 24-hour period were the רבנן worried about ruining pure items, but not for the shorter period from examination to examination. So the משנה teaches us that it applies there too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The משנה needed to spell out the shorter period because we could have guessed it works differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בדיקה shortens the time because the רבנן did not want to ruin too many pure items, called טהרות. Over a long 24-hour span, many טהרות could be ruined, so the concern is strong. One might think that over the short span between examinations there is little to lose, so the רבנן would not bother. The משנה tells us that the בדיקה shortens even this short span.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said: introduces a mistaken assumption the text comes to correct
They were concerned
Loss of pure items, meaning pure food or objects becoming טמא
It teaches us: the text includes this to rule out the mistaken assumption

phrases.english: Lest you say:
With regard to a twenty-four-hour period,
the Sages were concerned about the loss of pure items,
but from examination to examination, they were not,
so it teaches us that they were.

steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows that the seemingly obvious line rules out a reasonable mistake
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The concern for lost טהרות applies only to the long 24-hour period, so a בדיקה would not shorten the short period.
steps.terutzMaskana: The concern applies to both periods, so a בדיקה shortens even מפקידה לפקידה.
steps.whatToRemember: A בדיקה shortens the window of retroactive טומאה both for the 24-hour period and for the period since her last examination. The goal is to avoid ruining טהרות.

steps.title: Why does the משנה mention the bed?
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's case of דיה שעתה, the גמרא asks why it says she was sitting on a bed, when it could just say she was handling טהרות and then saw blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה explains 'her time is enough' with a woman who was sitting on a bed handling pure items. Why mention the bed? It could just say she was handling pure items, stepped away, and saw blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה. It asks why the משנה adds the detail of the bed, which seems extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman with a fixed cycle is דיה שעתה. She becomes טמאה only from the moment she sees blood, with no retroactive טומאה. To show this, the משנה only needed to say the טהרות she handled stay pure. Adding the bed seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Her time is enough: she is טמאה only from when she saw blood, not retroactively
Ritually pure food or items
Why do I need it? Asks why a detail is included
And she stepped away

phrases.english: How is her time sufficient? And so on.
Why do I need it to teach:
She was sitting on the bed
and engaged in handling pure items?
Let it teach: She was engaged in handling pure items
and she left and saw blood!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new phrase of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's mention of the bed in the case of דיה שעתה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling about טהרות could be taught without the bed, so the bed seems like an extra detail.

steps.title: The bed teaches that a מעת לעת woman makes the bed טמא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the bed is mentioned to teach that it stays pure only because of דיה שעתה. When there is retroactive מעת לעת טומאה, the bed also becomes טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches us that the bed stays pure only because her time is enough. But when she is טמאה retroactively for 24 hours, the bed also becomes טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the purpose of the bed detail. It teaches a rule we learn by inference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה mentions the bed to show that it stays pure only because of דיה שעתה. From this we infer the opposite case. When a woman's טומאה goes back מעת לעת, she makes not only the טהרות טמא but also the bed she sat on during that time.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason, meaning only because of this
Bed
Becomes טמא

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the bed is just part of the story. The bed comes to teach that retroactive מעת לעת טומאה also reaches the bed.

phrases.english: This teaches us:
The reason the bed stays pure is that her time is sufficient,
but where she is impure for a retroactive twenty-four-hour period,
the bed is also rendered impure.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that a seemingly extra detail teaches a hidden rule by inference
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bed is an unnecessary detail.
steps.terutzMaskana: The bed teaches that retroactive מעת לעת טומאה makes the bed טמא too.
steps.whatToRemember: The bed stays pure only because of דיה שעתה. With retroactive מעת לעת טומאה, the bed becomes טמא too.

steps.title: This supports זעירי's ruling on bed and chair
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says this inference supports זעירי. He ruled that a נדה's מעת לעת period makes a bed and chair טמא strongly enough to make a person and his clothes טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports זעירי, who said: the 24-hour retroactive period of a נדה makes her bed and chair טמא. They become strong enough to make a person טמא, and that person makes his clothes טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that what we just learned from the משנה backs up an earlier ruling of זעירי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זעירי ruled that the retroactive מעת לעת period works like real נדה טומאה for a bed and chair. They become a משכב ומושב, which makes a person טמא, and that person then makes his clothes טמא. The משנה's bed detail shows the bed does become טמא in a מעת לעת case, which fits זעירי's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Supports: a source that backs up someone's opinion
Something lain on or sat on by a נדה, which becomes a strong source of טומאה
To make a person טמא, so that he makes his clothes טמא
A woman who is טמאה because of menstrual blood

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that retroactive מעת לעת טומאה is serious. It does more than make טהרות doubtful. It can make bedding a strong source of טומאה.

phrases.english: This supports Ze'eiri,
as Ze'eiri said:
The twenty-four-hour period of a menstruating woman
renders a bed and a seat impure,
to the extent of making a person impure,
so that he makes his garments impure.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the person who touches the bed or seat. He becomes טמא, and while still touching it, he makes the clothes he's wearing טמא too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the inference from step 4 to support זעירי.
steps.raayaObject: זעירי's ruling that מעת לעת טומאה makes a bed and chair טמא as a משכב ומושב
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's mention of the bed, which implies that the bed becomes טמא in a מעת לעת case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מעת לעת שבנדה עושה משכב ומושב לטמא אדם לטמא בגדים

steps.title: A bed cannot be asked, so its doubt should be pure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges זעירי. A bed is something that cannot be asked, and a doubt about such a thing is pure. So how can the bed become טמא through the doubtful מעת לעת period?
steps.simpleTranslation: Look, this bed has no mind that could be asked a question. And anything with no mind to be asked is ruled pure when there is a doubt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks זעירי's ruling from Step 5, which said the bed becomes טמא during the מעת לעת period.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The טומאה from מעת לעת is only a doubt, because maybe the blood really came out earlier and maybe it didn't. There is a known rule: a doubt about a thing that 'cannot be asked' (has no understanding) is ruled pure. A bed is exactly that kind of thing, so it seems it should stay pure.

keyTerms.meaning: Look now / after all. It opens a point that seems obvious.
Something with no understanding that could be asked about what happened, like an object or an animal.
When there is a doubt about it, it is ruled pure.

steps.confusionAlert: 'Being asked' does not mean we actually question the bed. It is a halachic category. Things with understanding (people) are treated one way in a doubt of טומאה, and things without understanding are treated another way: their doubt is pure.

phrases.english: Now look, this bed

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ דַּעַת לִישָּׁאֵל הוּא,
phrases.english: is a thing that has no mind to be asked,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ דַּעַת לִישָּׁאֵל
phrases.english: and anything that has no mind to be asked
its doubt is pure!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדִי הַאי מִטָּה דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ דַּעַת לִישָּׁאֵל הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges זעירי's ruling, which was just brought as support in Step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: זעירי's ruling that a נדה's מעת לעת period makes a bed טמא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A bed has no mind to be asked, and a doubt about such a thing is pure, so the doubtful retroactive טומאה should not affect it.

steps.title: זעירי meant when her friends carry her in the bed
steps.stepSummary: זעירי explains that he was talking about a case where her friends were carrying her in the bed. Then the bed counts as part of their hands, which do have a mind to be asked.
steps.simpleTranslation: זעירי explained his ruling: it is talking about when her friends are carrying her in the bed, so the bed counts as the hand of her friends.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by limiting זעירי's ruling to a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If people are holding the bed, the bed is like an extension of their hands. Since people do have a mind to be asked, the doubt is treated as a doubt about something that can be asked, and so it is טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: He explained it, meaning he set it in a specific case.
The hand of her friends. The bed is treated as part of the people holding it.

phrases.english: זעירי explained it
as a case where her friends are carrying her in the bed,
so that it counts as the hand of her friends.
phrases.notes: The friends are people who could be asked, so the bed takes on their status.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּרְגְּמַהּ זְעֵירִי כְּשֶׁחַבְרוֹתֶיהָ נוֹשְׂאוֹת אוֹתָהּ בַּמִּטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 6 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bed stands alone, has no mind, and its doubt should be pure.
steps.terutzMaskana: The bed is being carried by people, so it counts as their hand and has a mind to be asked.

steps.title: With רבי יוחנן's rule, no carrying is needed
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: according to רבי יוחנן, a doubt of טומאה caused by a person is treated as 'can be asked,' even for an object lying on the ground. So זעירי's ruling works even when no one is carrying her in the bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And now that רבי יוחנן has said that a doubt of טומאה that comes through a person's hands is treated as something we can ask about, even if it is a vessel lying on the ground, like something with a mind to be asked, זעירי's ruling holds even if her friends are not carrying her in the bed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a broader answer. It uses רבי יוחנן's rule so that זעירי's ruling no longer needs the special carrying case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What matters, according to רבי יוחנן, is not whether the object itself has understanding but whether a person caused the possible טומאה. Here the woman herself brings the possible טומאה to the bed. So even a plain bed counts as 'can be asked,' and the doubt is טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: And now that... It introduces a new answer based on a later teaching.
A doubt of טומאה that comes about through a person's action.
We ask about it, meaning it is treated like a case that can be asked, so the doubt is טמא.
A vessel resting on the ground, an object with no mind of its own.

steps.whyThisMatters: This moves the focus from what the object is to how the possible טומאה came about. That idea now becomes the center of the discussion.

phrases.english: And now that Rabbi Yochanan has said:
A doubt of impurity that comes through a person's hands
is treated as something we can ask about,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ בִּכְלִי מוּנָּח עַל גַּבֵּי קַרְקַע
phrases.english: even with a vessel lying on the ground
it is like something that has a mind to be asked,
then even though her friends are not
carrying her in the bed [the bed is still impure].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, wider answer to Step 6, which makes the narrow case of Step 7 unnecessary.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applying a general rule from another אמורא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: זעירי's ruling works only if people are carrying the bed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the woman causes the possible טומאה, the bed counts as 'can be asked' even when it is just standing there.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's rule stated on its own
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to רבי יוחנן's statement itself: a doubt of טומאה caused by a person is treated as 'can be asked,' even for a vessel on the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the statement itself. רבי יוחנן said: a doubt of טומאה that comes through a person's hands is treated as something we can ask about. Even a vessel lying on the ground is like something with a mind to be asked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets רבי יוחנן's rule out on its own so it can examine it. This is a setup for the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word גופא tells us the גמרא is leaving the topic of זעירי and the bed for now. It goes back to a statement it mentioned in passing, so it can test that statement directly.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The thing itself.' The גמרא returns to look closely at a statement it quoted in passing.

phrases.english: Now to the matter itself: Rabbi Yochanan said:
A doubt of impurity that comes through a person's hands
is treated as something we can ask about,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ בִּכְלִי הַמּוּנָּח עַל גַּבֵּי קַרְקַע
phrases.english: even with a vessel lying on the ground,
it is like something that has a mind to be asked.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the rule used in Step 8 and makes it the new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A doubt of טומאה brought about by a person is treated as 'can be asked' (so it is טמא), even when the object has no mind of its own.

steps.title: The case of the man wrapping himself in his cloak
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. A man wraps himself in his cloak near pure and impure items. If it is unsure whether the cloak touched them, the items are pure. Only if touching was unavoidable are they טמא. This seems to go against רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: If a man was wrapping himself in his cloak, and there were pure and impure items beside him, or pure and impure items above his head, and it is unsure whether he touched them or not, the items are pure. But if he could not have wrapped himself without touching them, they are טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that seems to clash with רבי יוחנן. This step sets up the challenge; the exact point of the clash is spelled out next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wrapping a cloak is clearly something a person does. So by רבי יוחנן's rule, a doubt about whether it touched the items should be טמא. Yet the ברייתא rules the doubt pure, and only calls it טמא when touching was certain.

keyTerms.meaning: Wrapping himself in his cloak.
Pure items and impure items.
It is impossible unless... meaning it definitely happened.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
If he was wrapping himself in his cloak,
and pure items and impure items were beside him,
or pure items and impure items were above his head,
and it is unsure whether he touched or did not touch
it is pure,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אִי אֶפְשָׁר אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נָגַע
phrases.english: but if it was impossible unless he touched,
it is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to test רבי יוחנן's rule from Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that a doubt of טומאה caused by a person is treated as 'can be asked.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Wrapping the cloak is a person's action, yet the ברייתא rules the doubt pure. That seems to contradict רבי יוחנן; the גמרא will spell out the exact point next.

steps.title: End of the cloak ברייתא: repeating the motion
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says we can ask the man to repeat the wrapping to see if he touched the items. The חכמים answer that we do not rely on a repeat in matters of purity.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: we tell him 'Do it again,' and he does it again. They said to him: we do not rely on repeating an action when deciding about pure items.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the quote of the ברייתא it started in the last step. This completes the source that the challenge against רבי יוחנן is built on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל suggests a test: have the man wrap himself again and watch whether the cloak touches the items. The חכמים reject this, because a second motion is never exactly like the first, so it cannot tell us what really happened. So for the חכמים, the doubt stays a doubt, and the items stay pure.

keyTerms.meaning: Repeat it (do the action again)
We do not rely on a repeated action to decide questions of purity
Pure items / matters of ritual purity

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
We say to him: "Do it again," and he does it again.
They said to him:
We do not rely on repeating in matters of purity.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: אוֹמְרִים לוֹ: ״שְׁנֵה״, וְשׁוֹנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted in step 10 as the basis for the challenge against רבי יוחנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: have him repeat the motion to check. חכמים: a repeat is not relied on for purity, so the doubt remains.

steps.title: Why are the items pure if a person caused the doubt?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the challenge: the doubt in the ברייתא was caused by a person, which according to רבי יוחנן counts as 'can be asked.' So the items should be טמא, not pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why are they pure? This is a doubt of טומאה that came about through a person!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא states the actual question against רבי יוחנן from the ברייתא it just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said that when a person causes the doubt, we treat the case as 'can be asked,' and a doubt in such a case is טמא. In the ברייתא, the man's own cloak may have touched the items, so the doubt came from a person. Yet the ברייתא rules the items pure, which seems to contradict רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Why? (asking for the reason behind a ruling)
A doubt of טומאה that was caused by a person

phrases.english: Why?

phrases.aramaic: הָא סְפֵק טוּמְאָה הַבָּאָה בִּידֵי אָדָם הוּא!
phrases.english: But this is a doubt of impurity that comes through a person!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי? הָא סְפֵק טוּמְאָה הַבָּאָה בִּידֵי אָדָם הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out the contradiction between the ברייתא just quoted and רבי יוחנן's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that a doubt caused by a person counts as 'can be asked' (step 9).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא the doubt comes from a person's cloak, so by רבי יוחנן the items should be טמא; but the ברייתא says they are pure.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about the public domain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: put that ברייתא aside. As רב הושעיא teaches, a doubt in a private area is טמא, but a doubt in a public area is pure. The ברייתא is talking about a public area.
steps.simpleTranslation: Leave that case aside, because רב הושעיא teaches: in a private area, its doubt is impure; in a public area, it is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן by showing the ברייתא is a special case that does not disprove him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate rules for doubts of טומאה. One is 'can be asked or not'; the other is where the doubt happened, private area or public area. Even if the case counts as 'can be asked,' a doubt that happens in רשות הרבים is pure, so the ברייתא fits רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Leave that one aside (it is a special case, not a real challenge)
Private domain
Public domain
Its doubt is treated as impure

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the ברייתא shows the case 'cannot be asked.' The גמרא agrees it can be asked, like רבי יוחנן said; it is pure only because it happened in a public area.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves רבי יוחנן's rule, which is the second answer for זעירי (step 8). So זעירי's ruling still works even when the bed is on the ground.

phrases.english: Except for that one,
as Rav Hoshaya teaches:
in a private domain, its doubt is impure,
in the public domain, it is pure.
phrases.notes: The גמרא assumes the cloak ברייתא happened in a public area, so the items stay pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּר מִינֵּיהּ דְּהַהִיא, דְּתָנֵי רַב הוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12 by limiting the ברייתא to the public domain.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (the ברייתא is about רשות הרבים)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the ברייתא's ruling of 'pure' shows that a doubt caused by a person does not count as 'can be asked.'
steps.terutzMaskana: The case can be asked, but since it happened in רשות הרבים, the doubt is pure anyway; רבי יוחנן's rule stands.

steps.title: Back to זעירי: what the מעת לעת period does
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now returns to examine זעירי's ruling itself: during the מעת לעת period, a נדה makes a bed and seat impure strongly enough to make a person impure, and that person makes his clothes impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: זעירי said: the twenty-four-hour period of a נדה makes a bed and a seat impure, so that they make a person impure, and he makes his clothes impure.
steps.whatsHappening: With the word גופא, the גמרא goes back to look closely at זעירי's statement on its own. This sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, זעירי's ruling was only mentioned in the middle of other questions. Now the גמרא quotes it in full: during the doubtful twenty-four hours, the bed and seat she used get the strong level of טומאה. They make a person who touches them impure, and that person also makes the clothes he is wearing impure.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself: the גמרא returns to examine a statement it mentioned earlier
The twenty-four-hour period back from when a woman sees blood, treated as a doubtful time
A bed she lies on and a seat she sits on
Making a person impure, and making his clothes impure too

phrases.english: The matter itself:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is going back to examine זעירי's words, which it brought up earlier.

phrases.english: Ze'eiri said:
The twenty-four-hour period of a menstruating woman
makes a bed and a seat impure,
to make a person impure, so that he makes his clothes impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about רבי יוחנן and returns to זעירי's ruling, first quoted in step 5, to analyze it directly.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During the מעת לעת period, a נדה's bed and seat become impure enough to make a person impure, and that person makes his clothes impure.

steps.title: Avimi's ברייתא seems to contradict זעירי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a נדה's bed and seat during the מעת לעת period are 'like her touch.' That suggests they do not make a person impure, which goes against זעירי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? When אבימי came from בי חוזאי, he brought a ברייתא: during the twenty-four-hour period of a נדה, her bed and seat are like her touch. Doesn't that mean that just as her touch does not make a person impure, her bed also does not make a person impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges זעירי's ruling from Step 14 by quoting a ברייתא that אבימי brought with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זעירי said that during the מעת לעת period, her bed and seat are strong enough to make a person impure. The ברייתא compares the bed to her touch. An item she touched during that period does not make a person impure, so the comparison seems to say the bed is weak too.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that really so? An opening that signals a challenge
The twenty-four-hour period before a woman found blood, when her impurity applies backward in time
Her bed and her seat, things she lies or sits on
Her touch, an item she touched
Is it not that...? The גמרא suggests how to read a source

phrases.english: Is that so?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא כִּי אֲתָא אֲבִימִי מִבֵּי חוֹזָאֵי,
phrases.english: But when Avimi came from Bei Ḥozai,
he came and brought a teaching with him:
phrases.notes: Here מתניתא means a ברייתא, a teaching from the time of the משנה that is not in the משנה itself.

phrases.english: During the twenty-four-hour period of a נדה,
her bed and her seat are like her touch.
Is it not that,
just as what she touched does not make a person impure,
so too her bed does not make a person impure!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָא כִּי אֲתָא אֲבִימִי מִבֵּי חוֹזָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges זעירי's ruling, which was just quoted in Step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: זעירי's ruling that during the מעת לעת period her bed and seat make a person impure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא compares the bed and seat to her touch. Her touch does not make a person impure, so the bed and seat should not either.

steps.title: רבא's קל וחומר: beds and seats must be fully impure
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects that reading with a קל וחומר. If a sealed clay vessel is not protected from a נדה during the מעת לעת period, beds and seats certainly are not protected.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Can you really think so? It is a קל וחומר. A clay vessel with a tightly sealed cover is protected in a tent with a dead body, yet it is not protected during the twenty-four-hour period of a נדה. Beds and seats are not protected even in a tent with a dead body, so surely they are not protected during her twenty-four-hour period!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back against the reading in Step 15 and shows by logic that beds and seats must be fully impure, as זעירי said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sealed clay vessel is stronger than beds and seats, because the seal protects it from a dead body's impurity. Even so, the seal does not protect it from the נדה during her מעת לעת period. So beds and seats, which have no protection even from a dead body, must certainly get her full impurity.

keyTerms.meaning: And can you really think so? A sign the reading is being rejected
A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter one
A clay vessel
A tightly sealed cover that protects a clay vessel from impurity
A tent or room with a dead body, which spreads impurity to what is inside
Saved, protected from becoming impure

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the מעת לעת impurity is treated as real and strong, so זעירי's ruling makes sense on logical grounds.

phrases.english: Rava said: And can you really think so?
It is a קל וחומר:
If a clay vessel
sealed with a tightly fastened cover,
which is protected in a tent with a dead body,
is not protected during the twenty-four-hour period of a נדה,
then beds and seats,
which are not protected in a tent with a dead body,
is it not logical that they are not protected
during the twenty-four-hour period of a נדה?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: וְתִסְבְּרָא? קַל וָחוֹמֶר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading of the ברייתא proposed in Step 15
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the bed and seat do not make a person impure
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That reading goes against a clear קל וחומר from the sealed clay vessel

steps.title: But Avimi's ברייתא still says otherwise
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: logic aside, אבימי quoted an actual ברייתא, and it seems to say the opposite of רבא's קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But אבימי from בי חוזאי is quoting a ברייתא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that a logical argument cannot simply push aside a written source like אבימי's ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's קל וחומר is strong, but the ברייתא is a real text. So we still have to explain what 'like her touch' means if it does not mean the bed is weak.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, an opening that presents a challenge

phrases.english: But Avimi from Bei Ḥozai
is quoting a ברייתא!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אֲבִימִי מִבֵּי חוֹזָאֵי מַתְנִיתָא קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on רבא's קל וחומר by pointing back to the ברייתא from Step 15
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A logical argument cannot override an explicit ברייתא, which seems to say the bed is only 'like her touch.'

steps.title: Rereading the ברייתא: 'her bed and her seat'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to reread the wording of אבימי's ברייתא so that it no longer goes against רבא. The rest of the answer comes on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: her bed and her seat...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer by offering a new reading of the ברייתא. The sentence is not finished here, so this step sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer will not drop the ברייתא. It will explain the phrase 'her bed and her seat are like her touch' in a different way that fits רבא's קל וחומר and זעירי's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead, a signal that the גמרא is offering a new reading

phrases.english: Say instead:
her bed and her seat...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question in Step 17 by rereading the ברייתא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Like her touch' meant the bed and seat do not make a person impure
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא will be read in a way that fits רבא and זעירי; the full reading comes next
